prize_parts.citation: for the invention of the optical lattice clock based on magic-wavelength trapping and its realisation at the 10^-18 level of fractional uncertainty

statement.case_for: I keep B036 as a single-part prize to Katori and Ye, with the same reasoning as in round 1 but sharpened by the exchange. Four members now reach it independently, and members who prefer other candidates (Danielsson, Mehlig, Eriksson) call its attribution the cleanest or name it as a fallback, so I do not need to lean on support counts. The scientific core is specific: Katori's magic-wavelength trapping removes the light shift on the clock transition while many atoms are interrogated in parallel, and the lattice clock then took fractional uncertainty to 10^-18 with independent confirmation in Sr, Yb and Hg on several continents. As an instrument builder I regard controlling lattice light shifts, blackbody and collisional effects at that level as a physical result about what can be measured, not a technique borrowed from earlier prizes. In answer to the chair's questions: the governing criterion should be a distinct, verified achievement with a clean credit, and on that criterion B036 is ready now while B022 has an open credit gap. The sentence I would defend is 'for the invention of the optical lattice clock based on magic-wavelength trapping and its realisation at the 10^-18 level'. It leaves to the 2005 and 2012 prizes the frequency comb and single-ion control, and leaves the ion clocks and the other lattice-clock groups' own results outside the citation. I would keep Ye's many-body and spin-exchange work out of the wording, as Olsson prefers, because it opens a second storyline and the record accuracy already covers his contribution. I find no two-part configuration viable within three names; every pairing with B036 forces B022, B054 or B046 into one name, which none of their supporters would accept.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unchanged: novelty against the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and credit shared with Lemonde, Gill, Takamoto, PTB, NIST, SYRTE, RIKEN and the ion-clock groups, which two names cannot capture. Danielsson, Mehlig and Eriksson are right that this must be argued, not assumed. My argument is that the magic-wavelength lattice is what allowed many-atom interrogation without a light-shift penalty, and that is a conceptual step beyond the comb and the single trapped ion, but it remains a judgement about lineage that reasonable members can weigh differently. A second weakness is that the result is 'another digit' of precision, as Olsson put it, rather than a new phenomenon, and the pending redefinition of the second has not happened. I do not want the prize to depend on that decision.

responses.point: Danielsson keeps B022 first because a sharp prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) was followed by a surprising, widely reproduced experiment (2018), and counts six of seven rankers placing it in the top three.
responses.response: I take the prediction-then-discovery structure as the strongest feature of B022 and I list it as my first alternative. But breadth of top-three placement tells me the candidate is widely admired, not that the credit is repaired. The decisive 2018 measurements were led by Cao, who is outside the three names, and earlier moire theorists also have claims. That is a gap in the configuration, not a gap in the science. Your own fallback list contains B036, and you say you would not oppose a precision-measurement prize. If the committee judges the Cao problem unrepaired, I read that as your path to B036 rather than a reason to wait on interpretation of the pairing mechanism.

responses.point: Mehlig argues that the unsettled pairing mechanism is not disqualifying because B022 rests on flat-band-driven correlated phases, and calls B036 a strong fallback if B022 is judged premature.
responses.response: Your distinction between honouring the existence of flat-band correlated phases and honouring a theory of the superconductivity is fair, and it weakens the maturity objection that I and others raised. I accept it. What it does not resolve is the credit. A citation that says openly it honours the prediction and the discovery still leaves out the first author of the experiments and several earlier moire band theorists, and the three-name limit prevents repair. On that point I find the clock configuration cleaner, and I am glad you hold it as a fallback. Evidence that would change my view: a convincing account of how Cao's role can be handled, or several years of settled interpretation.

responses.point: Kroll supports B036 and flags a possible recusal question because of his doctoral research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, linked to Ye's group lineage.
responses.response: I agree with your position on the science and on not tying the prize to the redefinition of the second. On recusal, a doctoral stay in a laboratory whose lineage later overlaps with Ye's group is a distant tie with no documented link to Katori or Ye, and I do not think it requires you to step back. I would still ask you to state it in the record, as you have, and I would note that the configuration does not depend on your vote: Lindroth, Olsson and I reach B036 independently, so an abstention would not change my judgement of the case.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B054 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) as a short chain from prediction to observation, while acknowledging the 2016 overlap, the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and thin support, and says he would take B036 seriously if the magic-wavelength idea is shown to be decisive.
responses.response: You ask for the decisive step in B036, and I think it is this: before Katori's proposal, trapping neutral atoms in light perturbed the clock transition and forced a choice between atom number and accuracy. Magic-wavelength trapping removes that trade-off, so many atoms can be interrogated at once and the statistics follow. That is a specific idea tested by two groups, not a refinement of the comb. On B054 I agree with Mehlig that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang omission cannot be repaired after Zhang's death, and with you that the 2016 overlap is real. I would treat B054 as an alternative at most.

responses.point: Lindroth would credit Katori and Ye for lattice clocks and would also include Ye's many-body and spin-exchange control as part of what made 10^-18 reachable.
responses.response: I accept that the many-body and spin-exchange control was part of the route to the record, and your expertise in atomic structure carries weight on the magic-wavelength condition. But I prefer a narrower citation. Naming many-body control would invite the question of why the thorium nuclear clock and the quantum-simulation work are not included, and it would blur the boundary with the 2012 and 2005 prizes that all of us say must be kept clear. The citation can rest on the lattice concept and the 10^-18 realisation, and Ye's systematics work is already within the second phrase.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct step from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes; this is a judgement about lineage, not a fact I can settle.
Whether Lemonde, Gill, Takamoto or the ion-clock groups have priority claims that make a Katori and Ye credit incomplete; I have not verified priority dates independently.
Whether Danielsson and Mehlig would accept B036 if the Cao credit gap in B022 is judged unrepaired; they have not said so directly.
Whether B022 will look premature or overdue once the interpretation of the correlated phases settles; I rely on my own reading of the field.
statement.conflict_note: As chair and an astroparticle experimentalist I have documented ties to PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur and a CERN doctoral background; these are adjacent to B012 and B017, neither of which is in my configuration. No specific tie to Katori, Ye or any other credited person is apparent from my profile, and my preferred configuration (B036) raises no conflict for me. I have noted Kroll's disclosed Hall-laboratory connection and have given my view above; it is for the committee to decide.
